_note: Hand-written market take, refreshed twice a day (~8am and ~8pm UTC) by a separate scheduled research pass. Not touched by scripts/sync.py's automatic hourly sync. This is the site's hero paragraph (first thing under the H1 title), shown under the 'Today's Call' label. Not financial advice.
text: Bitcoin just ripped to $81,000, up nearly 6% in a day, as a short squeeze (over $180 million in liquidations) met real relief once the Fed's rate hike and the CLARITY Act's Senate failure both landed without breaking the market. Sentiment flipped fast too, with the Fear and Greed Index jumping from 56 to 71 as layer-2 and DeFi tokens led the broader rally. It's a genuine bullish signal, but moves built on squeezed shorts tend to run hot and cool off, so treat $80,000 as the support to watch, $84,000 to $86,000 as the next test if momentum holds, and a fast break under $78,000 as the sign the squeeze is over. The real confirmation to watch for is ETF flows turning positive again, since that's money walking in rather than shorts walking out. Either way, this is a read on where things stand, not a bet to make on its own.
